articles.title: Street Fighter review – nostalgia only goes so far in junky fighting game movie
articles.summary: There are brief, simple pleasures in the inevitable new big screen take on the classic game but like the recent Mortal Kombat movies, it’s a largely incoherent mess. We just had Resident Evil, Zach Cregger’s giddy, nasty, devilishly fun spin on Capcom’s popular zombie franchise.
body: But now here comes Street Fighter, a garish and incoherent mess that amuses in fits and starts but barely improves on the Mortal Kombat movies before it, crushing those hopes in its atomic suplex.

Fans certainly won’t mind. They’ve kept the box office’s life bar in the green for these one-on-one fighter adaptations going all the way back to the disastrous 1994 Street Fighter movie starring Jean-Claude Van Damme and his $10,000-a-week coke problem. They’ll happily tolerate how the new Street Fighter, like those Mortal Kombat movies, can barely string together a cohesive plot, which has clearly been pencilled in as an afterthought between rounds of combat in yet another tournament-style narrative. None of that will matter because they’re just here for the dopamine hits by way of nostalgia.

articles.title: Cult venue Prince Charles cinema ‘saved’ after lease renewal signed
articles.summary: The much-loved central London institution, which has been threatened with closure since January 2025, secures 25-year lease without break clause with current landlords.
body: The celebrated Prince Charles repertory cinema in London’s Leicester Square has announced that the threat of closure has been staved off by signing a new 25-year lease with its landlords.

In a post on social media titled “You Saved the PCC”, the cinema said that “after 21 months of uncertainty, we’re delighted to have secured the future of the cinema” and that they had “signed a new 25-year lease with no break clause, ensuring our projectors will keep rolling for years to come”.
The cinema also expressed its gratitude for the “support, commitment and belief of many, many people”.

In January 2025, the Prince Charles launched a petition, claiming that its landlord, Zedwell LSQ Ltd (owned by developer Criterion Capital) was trying to “bully us out of the building” by demanding a break clause in its lease, due for renewal in September 2025. The break clause would have enabled Zedwell to give the cinema six months’ notice if it had other plans for the site. At the time, Criterion Capital denied that it was attempting to intimidate or disadvantage the cinema.

articles.summary: Verve has signed a new 10-year lease for its worldwide headquarters in the Hollywood Media District, marking a significant commitment to the Los Angeles entertainment economy.
body: Located across from Sunset Las Palmas Studios, Verve’s HQ is situated alongside companies including Netflix, All3Media, Formosa Group, Paramount, SiriusXM and Roc Nation.

Founded in 2010, Verve is an independent talent and literary agency with operational divisions spanning motion picture literary, television literary, talent, non-fiction, media rights & publishing, Verve Ventures, commercial endorsements and digital. Verve clients include actors like Matthew Lillard, Keith David, Sean Bean, Olivia Thirlby and Eliza Coupe and filmmakers like Sara Hess, Ben Leonberg, Zeb Wells and Adam Stein.

articles.title: ‘Stranger than stranger-than-fiction’: how Lance Oppenheim made the year’s two buzziest films
articles.summary: Primetime and You Can See Everything are both clammy, audacious awards contenders that challenge our sense of reality. Ahead of the release of his drama starring Robert Pattinson as a TV vigilante, the 30-year-old director talks crime, punishment and South Park.
body: When I meet Oppenheim in a London hotel, it is to discuss his other hot ticket, Primetime, for which Robert Pattinson is the one attracting Oscar buzz. The Batman actor gives a high-wire performance as Chris Hansen, the sensationalist US television vigilante renowned for ambushing paedophiles on To Catch a Predator, which was a disreputable and highly addictive segment of the current affairs show Dateline NBC between 2004 and 2007. Hansen later parlayed the idea, and his crusading shtick, into a succession of spin-offs. Some, including Hansen Vs Predators, had the same sleazy catnip quality. Others, such as a sting to collar bicycle thieves, did not.

articles.title: Daniel Henney Joins Apple TV’s ‘Disavowed’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Daniel Henney has joined the cast of Apple TV’s upcoming action thriller “Disavowed.” Per the longline, “Disavowed” follows “legendary CIA case officer Brad Griffin, who is abruptly fired in the middle of a global hunt for an elusive assassin responsible for killing his colleague.
body: Daniel Henney has joined the cast of Apple TV ’s upcoming action thriller “ Disavowed.”

Henney’s previous works include starring as Lan Mandragoran opposite Rosamund Pike in Prime Video’s “The Wheel of Time.” The American actor got his start in Korea with the 2005 romantic comedy-drama “My Lovely Sam-Soon.” He later starred in “Criminal Minds: Beyond Borders” and “Criminal Minds.” His film credits include “Missing, X-Men Origins: Wolverine” and “Big Hero 6,” in which he voiced Tadashi Hamada. He also voices Jinn in the English version of the Netflix series “Genie, Make a Wish.”

The “Disavowed” series was originally announced back in May with Marsden in the lead role. The release date is yet to be announced. It is created and executive produced by Art Marcum and Matt Holloway. Tom Spezialy and Marsden will also executive produce. Blue Marble Pictures produces, with Theresa Kang and Caroline Garity serving as executive producers. Apple Studios will also produce.
Henney is represented by Buchwald, More Medavoy Management and Toczek Suddleson Law Group.

articles.title: ‘Don’t do this!’ Why Paul McCartney cares about looking shorter than John Lennon in Sam Mendes’ Beatles films
articles.summary: You’re Paul McCartney. So how come you’re still getting het up at a fictional version of you being marginally smaller than a fictional version of John Lennon? There has been a lot of discourse and conjecture surrounding Sam Mendes’s forthcoming Beatles biopics.
body: But until now the remaining Beatles have managed to keep fairly quiet about the whole thing. Last year Ringo Starr mentioned that he’d sat down with Mendes to rework a scene he wasn’t happy with, and Paul McCartney has praised the guitar playing of Paul Mescal, but it appeared that no real red lines had been crossed. Until now.

On the most recent episode of Amy Poehler’s podcast, McCartney hinted at one underlying tension that might just rip the whole project apart: under no circumstances should he be seen to be shorter than John Lennon.

Informing Poehler that he, Lennon and George Harrison were all roughly equal height – with Starr slightly smaller – McCartney revealed that he was moved to text Mendes after shots of the actors recreating the Abbey Road album cover were published. In them, it looked an awful lot like Harris Dickinson (playing Lennon) loomed above Mescal’s McCartney. As per McCartney’s retelling, the text read “Sam! Smaller? Don’t do this! You said you wouldn’t do it!”

articles.title: IShowSpeed Partners With Breakwater Studios, Obamas’ Higher Ground to Bring ‘The Eyes of Ghana’ Doc to Theaters (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Streaming superstar IShowSpeed has partnered with Breakwater Studios and Barack and Michelle Obama’s Higher Ground to bring Ben Proudfoot’s upcoming documentary “The Eyes of Ghana” to theaters for a one-night-only screening on Oct. 28, Variety can reveal exclusively.
body: IShowSpeed’s involvement in “The Eyes of Ghana” is just the latest example of digital creators mobilizing their audiences to movie theaters. Back in January, YouTuber Mark Fischbach, aka Markiplier, directed, starred in and self-distributed his sci-fi horror film “Iron Lung.” Not only did his fans call theater chains to encourage them to screen the movie, but they also showed out in droves on release day. The film opened to $17 million and ended its run with $50 million worldwide against a budget of just $3 million.

“Chris Hesse spent more than six decades documenting and safeguarding an extraordinary chapter of Ghanaian and African history,” stated Ethan Lewis, head of non-fiction at Higher Ground. “Higher Ground is proud to partner with IShowSpeed, Ben Proudfoot and Breakwater Studios and this accomplished team of artists to bring this remarkable story to theaters on Oct. 28th. ‘The Eyes of Ghana’ speaks to the power of film to preserve our collective memory, and to the responsibility we share in making sure these stories reach the next generation.”

articles.title: Mike Leigh Gets Standing Ovation at London Homecoming Premiere of ‘Tender Loving Care,’ Likely His Final Film
articles.summary: U.K. audiences aren’t usually ones to give standing ovations, but when one of their most cherished filmmakers makes a final bow, unwritten rules are allowed to be broken.
body: This was certainly the case for Mike Leigh, who on Thursday received a hero’s welcome at the London Film Festival premiere of “ Tender Loving Care,” a film he’s said will likely be his last.

Starring Kate O’Flynn, Marion Bailey and Paul Jesson, “Tender Loving Care” — set and shot in London — explores themes of aging, grief and relationships, while casting a harsh light on the underfunded British health and welfare system. The film premiered at Telluride and won both the top prize at the San Sebastian Film Festival and best leading actor award for O’Flynn.

Speaking via video in San Sebastian and echoing comments he’d made earlier, Leigh said the film was “more than likely” his final film due to his own health issues. “It’s quite straightforward, I have a medical condition [myositis], which affects my muscular movement, and it’s quite difficult to move around,” he said. “[It’s] certainly more difficult than it should be for a filmmaker, and therefore it’s more than probable that this film will have to be my last film. That’s all.”
He added: “It’s a practical matter to do with my medical condition — a physical condition.”

articles.title: Russell Brand accuser says he turned 'monster-like' before alleged rape
articles.summary: The 51-year-old faces three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.
body: A woman who alleges Russell Brand raped her in a hotel room has said he turned from "camp, friendly and effeminate" to "monster-like" before the alleged assault.
The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies the charges.
One of the women told the jury at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday: "He was just dark and arrogant and performing - he was scary, he was demanding."
The woman told police she met Brand before he was famous while attending the Labour Party conference in Bournemouth in 1999. She alleges he later raped her.

articles.title: Prepare to Fall in Love With ‘Sense and Sensibility’ Star Herbert Nordrum
articles.summary: The Norwegian actor — heart-wrenching as the lovesick Colonel Brandon — sits down to talk pleasing Jane Austen fans, his chemistry with Esmé Creed-Miles and the legacy of the late Alan Rickman: "It's very important to recognize the shoulders I stand on."
body: Herbert Nordrum chooses the funniest — and, ironically, maybe most British — possible allegory when describing his involvement in Georgia Oakley’s Sense and Sensibility. “It feels like I’ve been dropped in the national English football team,” the Norwegian tells The Hollywood Reporter. “And everyone is passing me the ball, and they’re not being weird about it.”

He hasn’t asked Oakley, but Nordrum’s hunch is that she spotted him in Joachim Trier ‘s The Worst Person in the World, his breakout feature, next to Renate Reinsve. At the top of our call, with Nordrum knee-deep in Sense and Sensibility press, we take a moment to reflect on the whirlwind success of that unsuspecting drama. “[Trier] deserves the position he’s in right now completely,” says Nordrum about his fellow countryman who, fast forward five years, is now an Oscar-winning filmmaker. “He’s just an amazing director — so playful, but at the same time, maybe the smartest person I know. And it’s the first time I felt someone valuing what I did,” continues Nordrum. “I learned a lot from him.”
